title: Adaptive Kernel Negotiator for Token-Phase Aware Mixed-Burst Serving
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Mixed-burst conversational workloads show large variance in sequence length and token-phase behavior (long prefill followed by short decode bursts). Static kernel-selection heuristics either overspend for short decodes or miss throughput on long-prefill paths, leading to 95p latency regressions and higher token cost. Goal: implement a negotiator component that picks per-request kernel execution paths via a lightweight two-phase probe + cache-aware policy, minimizing 95th percentile latency without regressing median cost. Approach: 1) Token-phase fingerprinting: compute a tiny signature from prefix tokens + model-last-activation stats to classify requests into phase buckets (early-prefill, steady-prefill, decode-burst). 2) Two-phase negotiation: quick micro-probe (≤1ms microbench) on a small submatrix or probe-case when unknown; otherwise skip probe and apply a cached policy. 3) Prefetchless fast-path: for decode-bursts, use a prefetchless low-overhead kernel variant to reduce tail latency at the expense of modest throughput for long streams. 4) Cache and TTL: policy cache keyed by (model, seq-histogram, token-phase) with TTL and eviction by frequency/latency. 5) Offline distillation: use collected telemetry to train a lightweight policy network (policy distilled to a small decision tree or linear model) for warm starts. 6) Safety and fallbacks: cost/latency cost model with guardrails; automatic rollback to conservative kernel on SLA violation. Success metrics: 95p latency down by >=12% for mixed-burst traces; median cost per token change <= +2%; misclassification rate for token-phase <= 8%.
acceptance_criteria: Experimental A/B shows >=12% reduction in 95th percentile latency on mixed-burst production trace (30-day window)
Median per-token cost change is within +2% of baseline or better
System falls back to conservative kernel within 200ms of detecting SLA drift or error spike
Policy cache hit rate >= 75% for steady workloads after 48 hours of rollouts
End-to-end canary rollout completed without increased error rate or infra instability
rollout_plan: 1) Dev experiments on staging with synthetic mixed-burst traces. 2) Canary to 5% traffic on runtime-1.21 with telemetry gating (95p latency / cost). 3) Ramp to 25% then 50% with automated rollback hooks. 4) Full rollout if metrics stable for 72h.
monitoring: Dashboards: runtime/negotiator-latency (p50/p95/p99), negotiator/cache-hit-rate, kernel-switch-rate, probe-latency, policy-body-size. Alerts: 95p latency > baseline+10% for 15m, cache-hit-rate < 50% for 30m, probe error rate > 0.1%.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive caching reduces probes but risks stale choices after model version changes — we will include model-version in cache key and bump TTL on rollout. Bandit selection deferred to phase 2 due to instability in early-stage production traces. Policy distillation uses offline telemetry and retrains nightly for stable workloads.
